steps.title: Relative clauses: choose the form from the relationship, not from English word order
steps.body: A relative clause lets you specify a person, thing or idea without starting a new sentence. Choose qui when the relative pronoun is the subject, que for a direct object, dont when the missing link would use de, and où for a place or time. After many prepositions, use lequel / laquelle / lesquels / lesquelles; with à and de, forms combine (e.g. auquel, duquel). Use ce qui / ce que / ce dont when there is no specific noun before the clause. Test the verb or expression: avoir besoin de → dont; s'intéresser à → auquel.

steps.title: Relative clauses: choose the form from the relationship, not from English word order
rows: Le cours qui commence en septembre est intensif.
The course that starts in September is intensive.
Le dossier que j'ai envoyé est complet.
The file that I sent is complete.
Les compétences dont elle a besoin sont précises.
The skills she needs are specific.
Le programme auquel je pense dure un an.
The program I am thinking of lasts a year.
ce qui / ce que / ce dont

steps.prompt: Choose the correct form: les critères ___ le programme fait référence.
steps.explain: Faire référence à takes à; with plural masculine critères, use auxquels.

steps.prompt: In ce qui me manque, what is qui?
options: The subject of the relative clause
steps.explain: Qui is the subject of me manque.
